name: Optcatch – Lead Capture, Email Campaigns & Newsletter for Any Form
author: eliastoss

sections.description:
Optcatch: lead capture, email campaigns and multi-SMTP sending in one WordPress plugin. It turns the forms you already run into an email list with a consent record for every contact, then sends newsletters and email campaigns from your own Gmail, Microsoft 365, SendGrid or SMTP account — with multi-SMTP sender rotation across every account you connect. Optcatch Pro adds drip autoresponders, re-engagement campaigns and automated email warm-up, so a new sending domain is far less likely to be flagged.

No list scraping, no third-party CRM, no per-subscriber fees. Every contact comes from a form submission on your own site or from a list you have confirmed permission to email, each stored with the consent basis, wording version and timestamp, and every send is checked against that record first. By default only visitors who tick a consent checkbox are stored (strict consent); you can instead choose to capture every form submission, and those contacts are recorded as captured under that policy, not as a ticked checkbox.

Lead capture from any form on your site

It doesn’t matter which form plugin, theme or page builder you use. Universal auto-detect is on by default and picks up any form with an email field – contact forms, newsletter boxes, popups, theme and page-builder forms, or hand-written HTML. Login, password, search and payment forms are ignored. You don’t need any code or a specific form plugin.

  • Any form, zero setup – Divi, Bricks, Beaver Builder, theme footers, popup builders, custom HTML: if it has an email field, it’s captured. Your form already has its own marketing opt-in checkbox? Add the class lcc-consent to it and the plugin reuses it as the consent gate.
  • Deeper integration with popular form plugins – on top of universal capture, Contact Form 7, WPForms, Elementor Pro Forms, Gravity Forms, Fluent Forms and Ninja Forms are also captured server-side, with their native consent/acceptance fields recognised and the form name recorded as the contact’s source.
  • WooCommerce – opt-in customers at checkout or account registration.
  • Webhooks & REST API (Pro) – send leads from external tools (Zapier, Make, Typeform, landing-page builders) to a secure endpoint protected by a secret key.
  • Shortcode form – no form yet? [optcatch_form] drops a clean, mobile-friendly signup form anywhere. It replaces the older shortcode names, which were removed in 0.9.20.

Multi-SMTP sender rotation, and automated SMTP warm-up in Pro

  • Daily limit and sending speed – every sending account has a daily limit and a per-minute speed you set yourself, so a campaign is spread out instead of going in one burst.
  • Email warm-up (Pro) – a new Gmail, Outlook or SMTP account starts at a safe daily volume (for example 50/day) and ramps up automatically as reputation builds. You set the start, growth and ceiling, and the next day’s higher limit only unlocks once a day has really used its allowance.
  • Multi-SMTP rotation – pool several sending accounts; campaigns rotate across them so no single account hits its provider limit.
  • Daily caps, pacing and a circuit breaker – hard per-account caps, paced dispatch over a sending window, and automatic pauses when a provider starts rejecting mail.
  • Gmail / Google Workspace OAuth2, Microsoft 365 / Outlook OAuth2, SendGrid API and any SMTP server – connect without storing raw passwords for Google and Microsoft.

Email marketing campaigns and newsletters

  • Campaign builder – branded newsletters with header, buttons, social links and simple formatting.
  • Templates – six starter designs (welcome, newsletter, product launch, follow-up, re-engagement, personal note) plus a drag-and-drop studio to save as many of your own as you like. Pro adds six more ready-made designs: event / webinar invitation, flash sale with coupon code, lead-magnet delivery, customer story, appointment confirmation & reminder, and a review request with one-click rating buttons.
  • Segments – filter by the form a contact came from, tag, signup date or consent status.
  • CSV import and export – bring existing subscribers in with tags and a recorded permission statement.
  • Delivery dashboard – live sent/failed/skipped counts per campaign and per sending account.

Wake-up follow-ups, drip autoresponders and re-engagement (Pro)

  • Wake-up follow-up (Pro) – every new contact is emailed automatically minutes, hours or days after they are captured. Drip / welcome sequences (Pro) – scheduled automation campaigns after capture.
  • Re-engagement (Pro) – the second touch for leads who never replied: weeks or months after capture, each quiet contact gets one win-back email with a reason to come back, recovering leads you already paid for without buying new traffic.
  • Reliable background delivery – a heartbeat, a token-protected tick URL for server cron, and a reconciler that unsticks any campaign.

GDPR consent engine

  • Consent audit trail – exact wording shown, wording version, UTC timestamp and source page per contact.
  • Explicit opt-in by default – a consent checkbox is added to captured forms (or your existing marketing opt-in checkbox is reused; a privacy-policy or terms box never counts as marketing consent); unticked submissions are not stored. An optional “Automatic Consent on Submission” policy captures every submission and records that policy as the consent basis.
  • Allowlist sending – the send query intersects a positive-consent allowlist and excludes unsubscribed contacts, always.
  • One-click unsubscribe – compliant link and List-Unsubscribe headers in every email.

Free vs Pro

The free version is complete on its own and has no usage limits: form auto-capture, CSV import (up to 5,000 rows per file), unlimited contacts, unlimited saved segments, unlimited custom templates, the starter templates, immediate sends, and as many sending accounts (Gmail, Microsoft 365, SendGrid or SMTP) as you like, each with its own daily limit, sending speed and automatic rotation. Optcatch Pro (a separate plugin from optcatch.com) adds features, not bigger numbers: automated mailbox warm-up, scheduled and delayed/automation sends, wake-up and re-engagement emails, the Pro template library (six extra ready-made designs), file attachments and hosted download links, webhooks & REST API ingestion from external tools (Zapier, Make, Typeform), and multisite licensing.

Optcatch Pro is a separate plugin, available from optcatch.com and not hosted on WordPress.org. It is installed on its own and keeps your contacts, campaigns and settings. This free plugin contains no Pro code and no license checks: nothing in it is locked or waits for a key, and no license key can unlock anything inside it. The Pro features exist only in Optcatch Pro.

External services

This plugin connects to the following third-party services. None of these connections
happen unless you actively opt in or configure the feature described.

  • Freemius — used for the optional opt-in and for Pro licenses. Nothing is sent to
    Freemius unless you choose to: (1) if you click “Allow & Continue” on the plugin’s opt-in
    screen, your name and email, the site URL, WordPress/PHP/plugin versions and this plugin’s
    activation/deactivation events are sent (the list of other plugins and themes too, unless
    you switch it off on that screen); (2) if you use Optcatch Pro (a separate plugin), its license key
    and site URL are sent to validate it; (3) if you fill in the optional feedback form when
    deactivating, the reason you choose is sent anonymously. If you skip the opt-in, nothing is
    sent. The free version receives its updates from WordPress.org.
    Freemius Terms of Service |
    Freemius Privacy Policy
  • SendGrid — only if you choose SendGrid as your sending provider in Settings. Each
    campaign/wake-up email (recipient address, subject, body, and any attachment) is sent via
    SendGrid’s Mail Send API instead of your server’s own mail transport.
    SendGrid Terms of Service |
    SendGrid Privacy Policy
  • Google (Gmail) — only if you connect a Google account for sending. The plugin uses
    Google’s OAuth2 flow to obtain and refresh a token used solely to authenticate outgoing
    mail via Gmail’s SMTP/API; your Google account email address is read to confirm which
    account is connected.
    Google Terms of Service |
    Google Privacy Policy
  • Microsoft 365 / Outlook — only if you connect a Microsoft account for sending. The
    plugin uses Microsoft’s OAuth2 flow and the Microsoft Graph API in the same way as the
    Google integration above, solely to authenticate and send outgoing mail.
    Microsoft Services Agreement |
    Microsoft Privacy Statement

Data this plugin collects, and when

Per WordPress.org Plugin Guideline 7, here is exactly what is stored and when.

From your visitors (only when they tick the consent box on one of your forms):

  • Email address, and any of: phone, first name, last name, company — read from your form’s
    own fields at the moment of submission.
  • The URL of the page the form was on (source_page).
  • Consent evidence: consent_status = opted_in, the exact consent wording shown, a wording
    version id, and a UTC timestamp.

If the visitor does not tick the box, nothing is sent or stored — the form submits
normally and the plugin ignores it. This is the default.

Optional “Automatic Consent on Submission” policy: if you switch to it under Settings, every
form submission is stored as above without a checkbox, and the consent evidence records that the
contact was captured under this policy (no checkbox wording is attached). You are responsible for
having a legal basis to email these contacts.

From you, the site owner (only when you import):

  • The contact fields you provide (email, phone, names, company, tags).
  • Consent evidence: consent_status = customer_declared, the permission statement you affirmed,
    and a UTC timestamp. The plugin also records that you checked the “I confirm I have permission
    to email these contacts” box, with a timestamp and your user id.

Sending / operational data:

  • Per-recipient send records (which campaign, which contact, sent/failed/skipped, timestamp).
  • Unsubscribe events (status set to unsubscribed with a UTC timestamp).

The plugin does NOT collect passwords, payment/card data, or other sensitive fields from
your forms — those field types are explicitly excluded from capture. By default, email is
delivered through your own site’s wp_mail() and no lead/contact data leaves your site. If
you choose to configure SendGrid, Gmail, Microsoft 365 or an SMTP server as your sending
provider, the recipient address and email content are sent to that provider to deliver the
message — see “External services” above for details.

Sample privacy-policy clause

You are responsible for your own privacy policy. You may adapt the following:

Marketing contact data. When you submit a form on this site and tick the marketing
consent box, we store the contact details you entered (such as your email address and name),
the page you submitted from, and a record of the consent wording you agreed to together with
the date and time. We use this to send you marketing emails you have consented to. You can
withdraw consent at any time using the unsubscribe link in any email, after which we will not
email you again. We do not sell this data or share it with third parties for their own
marketing. To request access to, or deletion of, your data, contact us at [your address].
sections.installation:
1. Upload the optcatch-lead-capture-campaigns folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the “Plugins” screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to “Lead Capture” in the admin menu. Review the consent wording under Settings.
  4. Forms are detected automatically: any form with an email field (Contact Form 7, WPForms,
    Elementor, page-builder, theme or custom HTML forms) is captured. If a form already has its
    own marketing opt-in checkbox, add the class lcc-consent to it (or to its field wrapper) and
    that checkbox becomes the consent gate. Import a list or start a campaign.
sections.faq:
Which forms does it work with?

Any form on your site that has an email field: form plugins, theme and page-builder forms (Divi, Bricks, Elementor…), popups and custom HTML. Universal auto-detect is on by default, so there is nothing to set up; in strict mode the plugin adds its consent checkbox to the forms it detects. If a form already has its own marketing opt-in checkbox, add the class lcc-consent to that checkbox (or its field wrapper) and the plugin reuses it instead of adding a second one. If you’d rather choose forms yourself, turn auto-detect off: then only forms you have marked with that consent class, plus the form-plugin integrations you switch on, are captured.

Can I send leads from Zapier, Make, Typeform or any other application into the list? (Pro)

Yes, with Optcatch Pro (separate plugin from optcatch.com). Pro adds a webhook / REST API endpoint with a secret key. Any application or third-party service that collects leads and can send an HTTP request can push them here: Zapier, Make, Typeform, Calendly, landing-page builders, a CRM, a chatbot, a lead-generation vendor, a mobile app or your own code. Each lead is created with its consent basis recorded, deduplicated and tagged, exactly like a form submission. Settings → Advanced Integrations shows the endpoint (/wp-json/optcatch/v1/lead), the key (sent in the X-Optcatch-Key header or as Authorization: Bearer), a payload reference and ready-to-use Zapier and cURL examples. Forms on your own site never need this.

Can it capture Contact Form 7 leads into an email list?

Yes – like every other form on your site. Contact Form 7 is also integrated server-side: its native [acceptance] field is recognised as the opt-in, and the contact is created with its consent basis recorded. No webhooks, Zapier or external CRM needed. Switch to “Automatic Consent on Submission” if you want every submission captured.

Does it work with WPForms, Elementor Pro, Gravity Forms and WooCommerce?

Yes. These are captured like any other form, and also get built-in server-side integration: WPForms, Elementor Pro Forms, Gravity Forms, Fluent Forms, Ninja Forms and WooCommerce checkout/registration.

What is SMTP warm-up (email warm-up), and does it warm up a new Gmail or SMTP account? (Pro)

Sending hundreds of emails from a fresh account gets it flagged as spam. Warm-up starts each account at a safe daily volume and raises the limit day by day (you set start, growth and ceiling) until it reaches full capacity. It works for Gmail, Microsoft 365, SendGrid and plain SMTP accounts.

How does multi-SMTP sender rotation work?

Connect several sending accounts. Campaigns are distributed across them within each account’s daily limit, so no single mailbox hits its provider limit.

How is this different from WP Mail SMTP or FluentSMTP?

Those plugins route your site’s transactional mail through one SMTP connection. Optcatch is an email-marketing tool: it builds the list from your forms, segments it, and sends campaigns through one or several sending accounts with rotation (automated warm-up is an Optcatch Pro feature). You can keep your SMTP plugin for transactional mail.

Can I send newsletters through Gmail or Microsoft 365 / Outlook?

Yes. Both connect with OAuth2, so no raw mailbox password is stored. SendGrid (API key) and generic SMTP are also supported.

Is it GDPR compliant?

It records a consent basis for every contact: the policy in force (inquiry or explicit checkbox), the wording version, a UTC timestamp and the source page, and sending always excludes unsubscribed contacts. In strict mode (the default) nothing is stored unless the visitor ticks the box. Whether your use is compliant depends on your legal basis and privacy policy; see ‘Data this plugin collects’ and the sample clause.

Can I set up automated drip or autoresponder emails?

Yes, in Optcatch Pro (separate plugin from optcatch.com). Automation campaigns deliver a welcome message or sequence a set number of hours or days after capture. The free version sends campaigns when you press send.

What is the wake-up / re-engagement feature?

Wake-up is available in Optcatch Pro (separate plugin from optcatch.com) and has two emails: a follow-up shortly after capture, and a re-engagement message for contacts that have gone quiet for a window you choose. Both are paced within your account limits.

Can a campaign accidentally email someone who unsubscribed?

No. Every send query intersects a positive-consent allowlist and excludes unsubscribed contacts. Unsubscribe status survives re-imports.

Does it work without buying Pro?

Yes, and there are no usage limits in the free version: unlimited contacts, saved segments and custom templates, CSV import up to 5,000 rows per file, campaigns, and any number of sending accounts with daily limits, sending speed and rotation. Automated warm-up, scheduled/automation sends, wake-up and re-engagement emails, attachments, the Pro template library (six extra designs) and the webhook / REST API endpoint for external tools are available in Optcatch Pro, a separate plugin from optcatch.com.

Will it slow down my forms or site?

Capture adds one lightweight server-side step per submission, and campaigns go out in paced background batches, so page speed is not affected.

Does this plugin scrape or buy email lists?

No, and it never will. Contacts come only from your own consenting visitors or lists you confirm you have permission to email.
sections.changelog:
0.9.26

  • Fixed: the unsubscribe link in the plain-text version of an email could open “This unsubscribe link
    is invalid”. Links were written as “text (url)” and some email services and mail apps counted the
    closing bracket as part of the link. Links are now written as “text “, and the unsubscribe page
    ignores stray characters added to the end of the link, so links in emails already sent work too.
  • Fixed: the Email Studio’s “Card Corner Radius” setting was lost when the template was saved, and
    emails always used 6px corners. The chosen radius is now saved and used in the email.
  • Fixed (Pro): a campaign email could go out before a wake-up email that was already due when two
    sending checks ran within a few seconds of each other (for example “Send now” right after the
    background check). Due wake-ups now always go first.

0.9.25

  • Fixed: in the Email Studio, typing into a text block’s box in the side panel was sometimes lost after
    clicking there from the email preview (and the other way round), so the change was not saved.
  • Fixed: the Guide and the Sending settings labelled extra sending accounts and sender rotation as Pro.
    They are included in the free version.

0.9.24

  • Fixed (Pro): when re-engagement emails were waiting, they took every free sending slot and
    campaigns could sit at “0 sent” for hours. Re-engagement emails and campaigns now take turns;
    wake-up follow-ups for new leads still go first.
  • Changed (Pro): automation emails (sent a set number of days after sign-up) now wait their turn with
    campaigns, oldest first, instead of always going ahead of every campaign.
  • Fixed: a campaign deferred because the daily limit was reached waited until midnight even after the
    limit was raised. Saving a sending account now lets deferred campaigns continue right away when
    there is room. The same now goes for Pro automation emails held back by the daily limit.
  • Fixed: an email that could not be sent because of the contact (for example an invalid address) or a
    broken template counted toward the account’s daily, hourly and per-minute sending limits although it
    never left the site. It no longer does.
  • Improved: every email the plugin sends (campaigns, test emails and Pro wake-up / re-engagement emails)
    now also carries a plain-text version next to the designed HTML version, made from the final email
    with links written out and the unsubscribe link included. This helps deliverability and readers whose
    mail app shows plain text only. Other emails on your site are not changed.

0.9.23

  • Fixed: in the Email Studio, clicking a heading or text block on the canvas and typing right
    away lost the typed text (the canvas redrew and dropped the cursor). The cursor now stays where
    you clicked.
  • Fixed (Pro): a wake-up or re-engagement email for a just-captured contact could be sent ahead
    of older contacts that were still waiting for theirs while sending was paced. They now go out
    oldest first.
  • Improved: the campaign list now shows how many recipients were skipped because they were no longer
    recipients when their turn came (unsubscribed, deleted or removed from the segment). A campaign
    whose contacts were all removed used to read “0 sent / 2 total” with no explanation.

0.9.22

  • Fixed: after an older version of the plugin had run again on a site that was already updated
    (for example an old zip uploaded once more), the next update stopped with “could not migrate its
    data to the new internal names” and switched the plugin off. The plugin now keeps that older
    data as backup tables, leaves your current data untouched, shows a one-time notice and keeps
    running. “Delete all plugin data” on uninstall also removes those backups.

0.9.21

  • Fixed: the Sending Speed (per minute) is now a per-account limit shared by every campaign,
    wake-up and background run. Two campaigns sending at the same time could each use the full
    speed, sending twice as many emails per minute as configured.
  • Fixed: when sending is paced, campaigns are now served oldest first. A campaign waiting for
    its turn could be overtaken by newer ones again and again and wait for hours; a paced campaign
    now resumes exactly when the next slot frees instead of re-checking every 5 minutes.
  • Changed: sending is now spread evenly across the day. An idle account still sends a small batch
    at once (up to its Sending Speed), then one email every few minutes (daily limit spread over 24
    hours) instead of the whole hourly allowance in the first minutes of each hour followed by a long
    pause. Follow-ups and small campaigns no longer wait up to an hour behind a large send; the daily
    and hourly limits are unchanged.

0.9.20

  • Fixed: the background job schedule was never created on a fresh activation (the one-minute
    interval was not registered before scheduling). Activation now registers it first, and the hourly
    fallback re-creates a missing schedule on its own.
  • Changed: every inline script and style is now an enqueued file, loaded only on the plugin’s own
    screens.
  • Changed: the free build contains no license checks and no Pro code. The Pro features (wake-up and
    re-engagement, scheduled and automated delivery, attachments, warm-up, the Pro templates,
    webhooks) exist only in Optcatch Pro, a separate plugin from optcatch.com.
  • Fixed: unslashed input and a dead test-email handler flagged by Plugin Check; the REST tick token
    is now checked in the route’s permission callback.
  • Changed: internal names now use the “optcatch” prefix (WordPress.org requires prefixes of at least
    four characters). Settings, contacts, campaigns, tables and scheduled tasks move automatically on
    the first page load after the update; if they cannot be moved, the plugin stays inactive, shows the
    reason to administrators and retries on every page load.
  • Breaking: the REST base path is now /wp-json/optcatch/v1/ (or /?rest_route=/optcatch/v1/...):
    webhook endpoints optcatch/v1/lead, optcatch/v1/webhook and optcatch/v1/capture, heartbeat
    optcatch/v1/tick. Update the URL in Zapier, Make and other webhook senders and in any server
    crontab that calls the tick. The lcc/v1 paths no longer exist. The X-LCC-Key and
    X-LCC-Tick-Token header names are still accepted next to X-Optcatch-Key / X-Optcatch-Tick-Token,
    and existing webhook keys stay valid.
  • Breaking: the Gmail / Microsoft OAuth redirect URI is now
    …/wp-admin/admin.php?page=optcatch-settings&action=optcatch_google_oauth_callback (Google) and
    …&action=optcatch_microsoft_oauth_callback (Microsoft). Add the new redirect URI to your OAuth
    app in Google Cloud / Azure before you reconnect an account; already connected accounts keep working
    with their stored refresh tokens.
  • Breaking: WP-CLI commands are now wp optcatch run-jobs and wp optcatch wakeup.
  • Breaking: filters and actions use the optcatch_ prefix, e.g. optcatch_lead_form_selector,
    optcatch_consent_checkbox_selector, optcatch_capability and optcatch_upgrade_url. Update
    custom code that hooks the old lcc_ names.
  • Breaking: the shortcode is now [optcatch_form]; the older [lead_capture_form] and three-letter
    shortcode names were removed. Replace them on pages that embed the form.
  • Unsubscribe links in emails sent before this update keep working.
  • Admin pages moved to admin.php?page=optcatch-...; old page=lcc-... bookmarks redirect.
  • Purge your page caches after updating: cached pages still carry the old form field names and
    script data.

0.9.19

  • Fixed: contacts captured from forms on your own site were tagged “webhook” even though they did
    not come from a webhook. They are now tagged “auto-capture”; only leads that arrive through the
    Pro webhook key (with no tags of their own) get the “webhook” tag. Existing contacts keep their
    tags; remove the old “webhook” tag from them in Contacts if you like.

Earlier versions: see changelog.txt in the plugin folder.

    screen, your name and email, the site URL, WordPress/PHP/plugin versions and this plugin’s
    activation/deactivation events are sent (the list of other plugins and themes too, unless
    you switch it off on that screen); (2) if you use Optcatch Pro (a separate plugin), its license key
    and site URL are sent to validate it; (3) if you fill in the optional feedback form when
    deactivating, the reason you choose is sent anonymously. If you skip the opt-in, nothing is
    sent. The free version receives its updates from WordPress.org.
    Freemius Terms of Service |
    Freemius Privacy Policy
  • SendGrid — only if you choose SendGrid as your sending provider in Settings. Each
    campaign/wake-up email (recipient address, subject, body, and any attachment) is sent via
    SendGrid’s Mail Send API instead of your server’s own mail transport.
    SendGrid Terms of Service |
    SendGrid Privacy Policy
  • Google (Gmail) — only if you connect a Google account for sending. The plugin uses
    Google’s OAuth2 flow to obtain and refresh a token used solely to authenticate outgoing
    mail via Gmail’s SMTP/API; your Google account email address is read to confirm which
    account is connected.
    Google Terms of Service |
    Google Privacy Policy
  • Microsoft 365 / Outlook — only if you connect a Microsoft account for sending. The
    plugin uses Microsoft’s OAuth2 flow and the Microsoft Graph API in the same way as the
    Google integration above, solely to authenticate and send outgoing mail.
    Microsoft Services Agreement |
    Microsoft Privacy Statement

Data this plugin collects, and when

Per WordPress.org Plugin Guideline 7, here is exactly what is stored and when.

From your visitors (only when they tick the consent box on one of your forms):

  • Email address, and any of: phone, first name, last name, company — read from your form’s
    own fields at the moment of submission.
  • The URL of the page the form was on (source_page).
  • Consent evidence: consent_status = opted_in, the exact consent wording shown, a wording
    version id, and a UTC timestamp.

If the visitor does not tick the box, nothing is sent or stored — the form submits
normally and the plugin ignores it. This is the default.

Optional “Automatic Consent on Submission” policy: if you switch to it under Settings, every
form submission is stored as above without a checkbox, and the consent evidence records that the
contact was captured under this policy (no checkbox wording is attached). You are responsible for
having a legal basis to email these contacts.

From you, the site owner (only when you import):

  • The contact fields you provide (email, phone, names, company, tags).
  • Consent evidence: consent_status = customer_declared, the permission statement you affirmed,
    and a UTC timestamp. The plugin also records that you checked the “I confirm I have permission
    to email these contacts” box, with a timestamp and your user id.

Sending / operational data:

  • Per-recipient send records (which campaign, which contact, sent/failed/skipped, timestamp).
  • Unsubscribe events (status set to unsubscribed with a UTC timestamp).

The plugin does NOT collect passwords, payment/card data, or other sensitive fields from
your forms — those field types are explicitly excluded from capture. By default, email is
delivered through your own site’s wp_mail() and no lead/contact data leaves your site. If
you choose to configure SendGrid, Gmail, Microsoft 365 or an SMTP server as your sending
provider, the recipient address and email content are sent to that provider to deliver the
message — see “External services” above for details.

Sample privacy-policy clause

You are responsible for your own privacy policy. You may adapt the following:

Marketing contact data. When you submit a form on this site and tick the marketing
consent box, we store the contact details you entered (such as your email address and name),
the page you submitted from, and a record of the consent wording you agreed to together with
the date and time. We use this to send you marketing emails you have consented to. You can
withdraw consent at any time using the unsubscribe link in any email, after which we will not
email you again. We do not sell this data or share it with third parties for their own
marketing. To request access to, or deletion of, your data, contact us at [your address].
